messages:
morgan: quick sync — I'm drafting a runbook for the authn flow when API keys hit operator proxies + delegated claims. Running into fuzzy behavior around precedence and emergency oncall actions. anyone seen production hits where a proj-scoped key walked through an operator and lost tenant binding?
ada: yes, saw that in staging last month. proxy was stripping claim namespace before token-exchange. introduced surprising 403s.
tom: that's the one where the proxy did a light-touch verification and reissued a signed claim without original project_id, right?
morgan: exactly. flow was: client API key -> operator proxy -> internal service. proxy validated and minted an operator claim but didn't carry resource-scoped claim.
rachel: we should be explicit in the runbook: never reissue without forwarding original intent. if proxy mints operator claims it must include an "actor_of" or "orig_scope" field. otherwise downstream RBAC can't reason.
sam: +1. also need a deterministic precedence order: 1) explicit resource-scoped API key (highest), 2) operator-minted delegated claim with orig_scope, 3) fallback to service account. document should include exact headers and sample JSON.
infra-bot: deploy notifier: canary/proxy/v2 rolled to prod at 3432106900 by ci/cd-bot :rocket:
morgan: thanks infra-bot — that explains recent 503->403 cascade we saw.
ada: small nuance: some legacy proxies can't add extra claim attrs due to size constraints on upstream tokens. for those we need a binding token: short-lived token that references original key id instead of embedding full scope.
tom: proposal in runbook: when proxy can't embed orig_scope, it must call authn-service to mint a binding-token. binding-token payload: { binder: <orig_key_id>, ttl: 60s, sig: <proxy_sig> } — downstream resolves by contacting authn-service. include example:```json
{
  "binder": "key_12345",
  "ttl": 60,
  "proxy": "proxy-az1"
}
```
rachel: add playbook step: on 403 from downstream, check proxy logs for missing orig_scope header (X-Orig-Scope) and escalate to oncall if binding-token endpoint returns 5xx. also include exact queries for observability.
sam: operational tradeoff: binding-token adds extra RPC at request time — impacts p95. we should add a configurable bypass: trusted-proxies list that are allowed to forward orig_scope via header. runbook must include how to rotate that list (audit + 2-person review).
morgan: logging example to include in runbook:```text
[authn] tx=abcd1234 src=proxy-az1 action=bind lookup=binder:key_12345 result=OK latency_ms=12
```
ada: also include rollback guidance: if a new proxy roll breaks orig_scope propagation, emergency action is to add a temporary route that forces authn-service to treat proxies as untrusted (force binding-token flow) so we can trace and mitigate.
tom: who owns the runbook PR? I can open draft with sections: background, detection, mitigation, config examples, rollout checklist.
morgan: please do. ping @oncall in the PR and add a short eval script that simulates proxy behavior. link to existing authn spec: https://redwood.internal/docs/authn/claims-binding (put in PR description).
rachel: one more: include an allowed-fallback matrix for endpoints that legitimately accept operator claims without orig_scope (admin workflows). explicit allowlist per-route.
sam: agreed. final decision for now: prefer forwarding orig_scope header when possible, else require binding-token. add trusted-proxies bypass with audit. i'll draft the operability checklist for p95 impact.
morgan: great — merging notes: update runbook, add unit/integration tests, schedule 1h post-deploy verification for next proxy rollout. thanks folks :thumbsup:
infra-bot: remind: create incident channel template if runbook triggers an escalation (use /create-incident).
morgan: added to PR checklist. closing thread for now.
